original_question: Is the syndrome associated with early-onset optic atrophy with spinocerebellar degeneration also associated with a mutation in the gene which has been previously reported in patients with mitochondrial membrane protein-associated neurodegeneration?

final_qi.question: Is the syndrome associated with early-onset optic atrophy with spinocerebellar degeneration also associated with a mutation in the gene which has been previously reported in patients with mitochondrial membrane protein-associated neurodegeneration?
final_qi.long_answer: Mitochondrial membrane protein-associated neurodegeneration (MPAN) is one of the neurodegeneration-with-brain-iron-accumulation (NBIA) disorders and is caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the C19orf12 gene.  Since the original description of MPAN, additional patients carrying C19orf12 mutations have been reported whose clinical picture is dominated not by iron accumulation but by an early-childhood onset of optic atrophy together with progressive spinocerebellar degeneration/ataxia, spasticity and peripheral neuropathy.  These reports show that the phenotype associated with C19orf12 mutations is broader than classic MPAN and includes the syndrome of “early-onset optic atrophy with spinocerebellar degeneration.”  Thus, the optic-atrophy-spinocerebellar-degeneration syndrome is indeed associated with mutations in the same gene (C19orf12) that had previously been described in patients with mitochondrial membrane protein-associated neurodegeneration.
